\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نوجوانی} (nowjavâni)}{نوجوانی (nowjavâni)}]{\fa{نوجوانی} (nowjavâni) — adolescence, the teenage years}

\label{lesson:FA-C333-nowjavani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a newborn baby, then the Persian for to bring up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نوجوانی}}
\textbf{\fa{نوجوانی}} (\emph{nowjavâni}) — \textquotedblleft{}adolescence, the teenage years\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{نوجوانی} \fa{فوتبال} \fa{بازی} \fa{میکردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar nowjavâni futbâl bâzi mikardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In my teens I used to play football.
\end{quote}

From \emph{nowjavân} \textquotedblleft{}a teenager\textquotedblright{}: \emph{now} \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} + \emph{javân} \textquotedblleft{}young\textquotedblright{}. The past continuous tells what you used to do.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nowjavâni} is built on \emph{nowjavân} \textquotedblleft{}a teenager\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{now} \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} and \emph{javân} \textquotedblleft{}young\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}. All of it is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowjavâni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowjavâni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nowjavâni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a newborn baby, then the Persian for to bring up, then say \emph{nowjavâni} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دانش} \fa{آموخته} (dânesh âmukhte)}{دانش آموخته (dânesh âmukhte)}]{\fa{دانش} \fa{آموخته} (dânesh âmukhte) — a graduate}

\label{lesson:FA-C333-danesh-amukhte}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to bring up, then the Persian for adolescence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دانش} \fa{آموخته}}
\textbf{\fa{دانش} \fa{آموخته}} (\emph{dânesh âmukhte}) — \textquotedblleft{}a graduate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{دانش} \fa{آموخته} \fa{رشته} \fa{پزشکی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U dânesh âmukhte-ye reshte-ye pezeshki ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She is a graduate in medicine.
\end{quote}

Formal; literally \textquotedblleft{}one who has learned knowledge\textquotedblright{}. The everyday word is \emph{fâregh-ottahsil}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dânesh âmukhte} is built from Persian \emph{dânesh} \textquotedblleft{}knowledge\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âmukhte} \textquotedblleft{}learned\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{âmukhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to learn\textquotedblright{}. Both are native words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dânesh âmukhte}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to bring up, then the Persian for adolescence, then say \emph{dânesh âmukhte} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سربازی} (sarbâzi)}{سربازی (sarbâzi)}]{\fa{سربازی} (sarbâzi) — military service}

\label{lesson:FA-C333-sarbazi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for adolescence, then the Persian for a graduate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سربازی}}
\textbf{\fa{سربازی}} (\emph{sarbâzi}) — \textquotedblleft{}military service\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرم} \fa{دو} \fa{سال} \fa{سربازی} \fa{رفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâdaram do sâl sarbâzi raft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother did two years of military service.
\end{quote}

From \emph{sarbâz} \textquotedblleft{}a soldier\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Sarbâzi raftan} is \textquotedblleft{}to do military service\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarbâzi} adds the suffix \emph{-i} to \emph{sarbâz} \textquotedblleft{}a soldier\textquotedblright{}, usually explained as \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} + \emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}one who stakes\textquotedblright{}: one who stakes his head. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{میانسالی} (miyânsâli)}{میانسالی (miyânsâli)}]{\fa{میانسالی} (miyânsâli) — middle age}

\label{lesson:FA-C333-miyansali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a graduate, then the Persian for military service.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{میانسالی}}
\textbf{\fa{میانسالی}} (\emph{miyânsâli}) — \textquotedblleft{}middle age\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{در} \fa{میانسالی} \fa{ورزش} \fa{را} \fa{شروع} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedaram dar miyânsâli varzesh râ shoru' kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father took up exercise in middle age.
\end{quote}

\emph{miyân} \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{} + \emph{sâl} \textquotedblleft{}year\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}. \emph{Miyânsâl} is \textquotedblleft{}middle-aged\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{miyânsâli} is built from Persian \emph{miyân} \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{} and \emph{sâl} \textquotedblleft{}year\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}. All of it is native.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیری} (piri)}{پیری (piri)}]{\fa{پیری} (piri) — old age}

\label{lesson:FA-C333-piri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for military service, then the Persian for middle age.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیری}}
\textbf{\fa{پیری}} (\emph{piri}) — \textquotedblleft{}old age\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگم} \fa{در} \fa{پیری} \fa{هم} \fa{هر} \fa{روز} \fa{کتاب} \fa{میخواند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedarbozorgam dar piri ham har ruz ketâb mikhând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Even in old age my grandfather read every day.
\end{quote}

\emph{pir} \textquotedblleft{}old (of people)\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{piri} is built from Persian \emph{pir} \textquotedblleft{}old\textquotedblright{}, a native word for elderly people, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
